note: Informational only (D9): not a bench/run.sh product, no baseline, no bench/targets.json entry, never compared across fingerprints. What each of exec::Options' three planning knobs is worth on this machine, measured by running the SAME program with that one knob off. Every configuration at B=1, tile 256, lane_tile 8; baseline and knob-off captures run back to back in one alternating sequence so load drift cannot land on the contrast (D63 section 2(f): a first run that did not do this made Stage A look 0.65x FASTER with pairing off, uniformly including slot 4095, the output copy).

knob_sweep.units: microseconds per run, summed over every profile slot

pairing_ab.comment: The dedicated A/B for the one knob D63 was commissioned to price. slot 4095 (the output copy, which no interpreter option can touch) stayed at 0.61-0.64 us across all six captures except one 0.88 us outlier, which is this control's own noise floor.

stage_a_search_ladder.comment: Extracted estimate over the fully-paired default plan's estimate, E0, B=1, tile 256, lane_tile 8. 'before_D62' is the row D62 committed in egraph_scale.json, measured under the pre-D63 model; 'after_D63' is the same command under this entry's model. Both columns are cost-model ESTIMATES, not wall clock.
stage_a_search_ladder.verdict: Still noise: 0.35-0.59% sits an order of magnitude inside the model's own 64.6% mean relative error on the domains an optimisation decision turns on. cross_stage_wins remains 0.

prediction_error.comment: Mean absolute relative error, every measured domain / domains >= 1% of their config's time. Target < 25% (PROBLEM.md section 7). Rows 1-2 share D48's own 15 captures; rows 3-5 use the fresh 21-capture grid, so the 2->3 step mixes the grid change with a new measurement session.

ladder.fit: + pairing contrast in the grid, fresh 21 captures, scratch priced on byte_ns
